title: Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy-Based Grain Mapping via Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Processing
content: STEM images are crucial for understanding the structure and composition of materials, which in turn helps in comprehending their properties and functionalities. Grain classification, a key task in STEM image analysis, involves identifying and labeling different grains in a crystalline material. Traditional methods rely on manual analysis by experts, which is subjective, inconsistent, and labor-intensive. However, advancements in machine learning (ML) and computing hardware have enabled the development of ML methods for analyzing STEM images on regular PC workstations [1, 2]. Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF), an unsupervised ML method, decomposes a non-negative matrix into two lower-rank matrices with non-negative elements, making it useful for dimensionality reduction and feature extraction in various scientific domains. This study explores the application of NMF for grain classification and mapping using regular atomic-resolution STEM images, aiming to automate the process and improve efficiency.
